name: Yuncheng Yanhu International Airport
before:
The airport for Yuncheng in Shanxi province, 11 km north east of the city centre. It served more than 600,000 passengers in 2010, ranking 62nd among Chinese airports.

The terminal numbering here is genuinely confusing and worth getting right. Terminal 1 is the domestic building, but it was originally called Terminal 2 when it opened on 27 May 2012. Terminal 2 is the international building, and it was built on the site of the old Terminal 1. So the numbers were effectively swapped, and older guidance will point a client at the wrong building.

Terminal 1 has six boarding bridges, 12 staffed check-in counters, 10 self-service counters and eight security checkpoints, with departures upstairs and arrivals and four baggage carousels below. Terminal 2 covers 28,000 square metres with five boarding bridges.

The runway is 3,000 metres, rated class 4D, with seven parking aprons.

The airport was formerly known as Yuncheng Zhangxiao Airport.
after:
The airport for Yuncheng in Shanxi province, 11 km north east of the city centre. It handled 2,873,454 passengers in 2025, ranking 70th among Chinese airports.

Its single runway is 3,200 metres long.

The airport's current name is Yuncheng Yanhu International Airport, and it has also been called Guangong Airport.
